continuity_scope: A deliberately narrow Russian/East Slavic literary-folklore witness, not a pan-Slavic corpus: tale no. 159, ‘Марья Моревна’ (Marya Morevna), in the scholarly 1984 edition of A. N. Afanasyev’s Народные русские сказки. The edition identifies its printed text as no. 159 and preserves a recorded tale variant. This pass makes no claim about South Slavic, West Slavic, Belarusian, Ukrainian, regional Russian, oral-performance, religious, or modern adaptation continuities.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Народные русские сказки А. Н. Афанасьева, vol. 1, Nauka, 1984, pp. 300–305; Fundamental Electronic Library (ФЭБ) digital scholarly edition

work_or_witnesses.work: Editorial description of the Afanasyev edition
work_or_witnesses.edition: ФЭБ bibliographic record for the 1984–1985 Nauka edition

coverage_rule: Include each individually named or uniquely designated acting agent in tale no. 159 who materially initiates, directs, assists, opposes, transports, revives, or undergoes a consequential action: Ivan-tsarevich; Marya Morevna; Koshchei Bessmertnyi; Ivan’s three named sisters; the three uniquely designated animal-form brothers-in-law; Baba Yaga; and the unnamed-in-personal-name but uniquely designated bee queen. Do not make places, the fire river, water, chains, horses, animal groups, weapons, unnamed parents, unnamed animal helpers, or generic categories into character nodes.
omissions: All other Afanasyev tale numbers, including other Koshchei, Baba Yaga, Firebird, dragon, revenant, household-spirit, and witch narratives.
Unnamed animal helpers, the unnamed foreign bird, lioness, Koshchei’s unnamed horse, Baba Yaga’s herd, parents, armies, places, artifacts, and waters in tale no. 159.

Ukrainian, Belarusian, Polish, Czech, Slovak, Slovene, Croatian, Serbian, Bulgarian, Macedonian, and other Slavic traditions; local Russian variants not represented by this printed text; living ritual and religious contexts; and all later literary, film, tabletop, and game adaptations.
uncertainties: ‘Slavic folklore’ is an orientation label in the corpus, not a single canon. This evidence only supports the particular Russian/East Slavic tale witness named here.
The tale’s orthography and English transliteration vary (Кощей/Кащей; Марья/Мария; Бессмертный/Bessmertnyi). Original Russian labels are retained where possible.

The animal-form suitors are uniquely designated by species/form rather than given personal names. They are included only because this one witness treats each as an individual marriage partner and acting helper; they do not establish a generic shapeshifter people.
Baba Yaga in this passage is a named/designated individual antagonist and keeper of horses. This does not support an identity claim about every Baba Yaga or an equation with a universal witch class.
evidence_basis: Primary tale text in a scholarly digital edition, with page-level locators. The bibliographic record identifies the edition and pages. The pass is complete only against the declared named-agent rule for no. 159.
